## BLOCKING — B1: g7/g8 probe-FAILURE disposition unspecified (fail-open)

D4 keys g7/g8 on probe OUTPUT, never on probe FAILURE. A non-zero rc from
`git status --porcelain` / `git worktree list --porcelain` (corrupt or
half-removed tree, damaged `.git` pointer, unreadable index) yields empty
stdout, which a naive implementation reads as "zero rows ⇒ clean" — and the
tree then flows into `cleanup_branch_src`, whose body is UNCONDITIONALLY
destructive past the gate: `worktree remove --force`, then
`shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)` REGARDLESS of the remove's
outcome, then `prune` (slurm.py:3863-3880). That destroys a tree whose
reproducibility was never verified — the K1 class, and a violation of the
body's positive-verified-evidence contract (disk-hygiene.md #2127: probe
failure ⇒ KEEP, "refuse rather than inflict").

Survives the planned suite: T1-T8 all use HEALTHY fixtures, so a fail-open
implementation passes every test AND the §6 dry-run (all 13 live trees healthy).

Required: one D4 sentence — any git probe failure (non-zero rc at g7 or g8, at
classification OR re-probe) ⇒ `kept — probe failed` + escalate, never treated
as clean — plus a T-case with a corrupted `.git` pointer asserting KEPT.
Also make `locked` an explicit base-gate keep: on git 2.34 a locked worktree
refuses single-`--force` removal, the rmtree still destroys the dir, and
`prune` skips locked registrations — leaving a stale registration that makes
the next `materialize_branch_src` `worktree add` FAIL, wedging that issue's
SLURM lane. (0 of 13 live registrations are locked today — spec hole, not a
live hazard. Independently re-confirmed by the orchestrator.)

## SUBSTANTIVE

- S1 (premise D): the planned disk-hygiene.md paragraph must EXPLICITLY
  reconcile the "NEVER delete store/ or eval_results/" rule's letter — the rule
  reads "repo-root OR worktrees" and the scratch IS a registered worktree — by
  stating the clean-tree condition as the reproducibility proof. Folds into the
  existing D7/§4 doc edit; no new work.
- S2 (premise E): §2 hand-verified cleanliness on only 3/13 sampled, but §6
  asserts 13/13 and K2 halts on any mismatch — a legitimately-dirty unsampled
  dir would fail acceptance with every gate CORRECT. Now empirically moot: the
  critic verified all 13 (clean incl. --ignored, registered, unlocked,
  terminal-status, mtimes Jul 15 → Aug 1, all ≥15 d). Upgrade §2 to the full
  13/13 table so K2 is well-defined. Data supplied; zero additional work.

## MINOR

- M1: §6's "(/ is at ~98% used / 23 GiB free)" is stale. Measured now:
  86% used, 135 GiB free (`df -h /` → `/dev/root 945G 811G 135G 86% /`).
  Still above the 85% EPS_VM_DISK_THRESHOLD default, so the "cron triggers
  promptly" claim survives. Orchestrator-confirmed.

## ALTERNATIVES — A1 (concern, not blocking): file the sparse follow-up now

The critic found, and the orchestrator independently confirmed, that
`RSYNC_INCLUDE_PATHS` (slurm.py) carries NO `eval_results` entry — the include
set is pyproject/uv.lock/src/scripts/configs/external-open-instruct/tests/
data-sft, and the comment at slurm.py:905-906 states outright "The exclude list
keeps the eval-result history + dashboards out of scratch". So the 7.8 GB
`eval_results/` dominating every scratch tree is materialized by `worktree add`
and then EXCLUDED from the rsync to the cluster — it is never used at all.
A sparse-checkout scratch would cut ~80%+ of the footprint AT THE SOURCE and
cut per-dispatch materialization cost. It does NOT replace the tier (accretion
is unbounded in issue count; killed launchers still leak whatever is
materialized), so janitor-first / sparse-follow-up is the right ordering — but
the follow-up should be FILED unconditionally, not gated on the tier "proving
insufficient" as §8 currently words it.

## CLAIMS THAT CHECKED OUT (verified against primary sources + live FS)

- A (D2 gate sufficiency): HOLDS except B1. Fixture-tested on this VM's git
  2.34.1 — an untracked file inside the nested `external/open-instruct` repo
  DOES surface in the outer tree's `status --porcelain` (0→1 rows), and
  `worktree remove --force` on the exact production shape (detached + populated
  mode-160000 gitlink) succeeds rc=0. In-flight-write risk is covered by
  g5(48h)+g6(/proc)+re-probe; the residual seconds-wide TOCTOU is the one
  #2127 already accepted.
- B (D1 home choice): honest, and UNDER-argued. worktree_audit.py's guard 4
  keeps only TRACKED changes — its own header says untracked generated files
  "do NOT block" — which is exactly the wrong semantics in front of an
  unconditionally-destructive remover.
- C (D3 awaiting_promotion): SAFE, for a stronger reason than the plan gives —
  `materialize_branch_src` step 2 UNCONDITIONALLY destroys any existing scratch
  at every dispatch (slurm.py:3940-3944), so no dispatch/follow-up/resume ever
  READS a stale tree; reaping an idle one is a pipeline no-op regardless of
  status. `fetch_results` merges into `<src_root>`, never into
  `~/.eps-slurm-src`. Risk class is strictly LOWER than the hf_dl caches the
  same status set already governs.
- D (eval_results deletion): numbers reconcile. 94,512 tracked vs 94,511
  `find -type f` — the delta is exactly one tracked SYMLINK
  (`eval_results/issue356/baseline`), which `-type f` excludes. Nothing
  untracked; `--ignored` = 0 rows on all 13.
- E (§6 falsifiability): well-specified in shape; evidence base widened per S2.
